subject: Simulating orthogonal responses in observed variable model

messages.author: fd248aedd6f929a2
messages.subject: Simulating orthogonal responses in observed variable model
parts:
I am trying to simulate data for a very simple model as follows below, with a dichotomous treatment (Trt) and two continuous responses. I would like the responses (Grazers1 and Grazers2) to be independent, but the simulated data has a large error covariance between the endogenous variables, despite my request that they be independent. Any thoughts? - Thanks, Jim Grace

## Sim Model
sim.two <- '
Grazers1 ~ -1.5*Trt 
Grazers2 ~ -0.8*Trt
Grazers1 ~~ 0*Grazers2
Trt | 0*t1'

## Generate data
set.seed(2)
simdat.two <- simulateData(sim.two, sample.nobs=10000L)

parts: By the way, I don't get this problem if all the variables are continuous. However, if I simulate data treating Trt as continuous, then convert to dichotomous prior to analysis, the error covariance returns. Puzzling.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Simulating orthogonal responses in observed variable model
parts:
Hi.  I was not able to run your code, perhaps because I am using an older version.  So, I simulated the data manually.

The full data generating model has two treatment variables.  The outcomes are a stochastic functions of a latent treatment variable, call it TrtLV and the observed treatment variable, TrtObs is a determinate function of TrtLV based on the threshold model.  Of course the outcomes will be unconditionally dependent because they both depend upon TrtLV but I assume that what you meant was that you want them to be conditionally independent when you condition on treatment.

They should be conditionally independent conditional on TrtLV (confirmed in model 1).  However, the data only gives you TrtObs which contains less information than TrtLV.  As a result, conditioning on TrtObs does not suffice to produce conditional independence (confirmed in model 2).  However, if one can model TrtObs using a latent variable to represent TrtLV, then conditional independence is recovered (confirmed in model 3).

Here is my code:


# Data Simulation
Nobs = 10000 # Sample Size
TrtLV <- rnorm(Nobs, 0, 1) # Latent Treatment
Grazers1 <- (-1.5 * TrtLV) + rnorm(Nobs, 0, 1) # Outcome 1
Grazers2 <- (-0.8 * TrtLV) + rnorm(Nobs, 0, 1) # Outcome 2
TrtObs <- rep(0, times=Nobs) # Observed Treatment
TrtObs[TrtLV > 0] <- 1
Nada <- rnorm(Nobs, 0, 1) # Random instrument
myData <- data.frame(TrtLV, Grazers1, Grazers2, TrtObs, Nada) # Data frame
pairs(myData) # Scatterplot matrix

mod1 <- '
  Grazers1 ~ TrtLV
  Grazers2 ~ TrtLV
  TrtLV ~~ TrtLV
  Grazers1 ~~ Grazers1
  Grazers2 ~~ Grazers2
  Grazers1 ~~ Grazers2
' # end mod1

fit1 <- lavaan(model=mod1, data=myData)
summary(fit1) # Covariance between Grazers1 and Grazers 2 residuals not statistically significant

mod2 <- '
  Grazers1 ~ TrtObs
  Grazers2 ~ TrtObs
  TrtObs ~~ TrtObs
  Grazers1 ~~ Grazers1
  Grazers2 ~~ Grazers2
  Grazers1 ~~ Grazers2
' # end mod2

fit2 <- lavaan(model=mod2, data=myData)
summary(fit2) # Covariance between Grazers1 and Grazers 2 residuals statistically significant

mod3 <- '
  Grazers1 ~ TrtObs
  Grazers2 ~ TrtObs
  TrtObs ~ Nada
  TrtObs ~~ TrtObs
  TrtObs | t1
  Grazers1 ~~ Grazers1
  Grazers2 ~~ Grazers2
  Grazers1 ~~ Grazers2
  Grazers1 ~ 1
  Grazers2 ~ 1
' # end mod3

fit3 <- lavaan(model=mod3, data=myData, ordered=c("TrtObs"))
summary(fit3) # Covariance between Grazers1 and Grazers 2 residuals not statistically significant



I could not think of a way to tell lavaan to treat TrtObs as an endogenous variable off the top of my head.  So, I added Nada as a useless predictor to render TrtObs endogenous.

Keith

Thanks Keith!

Much appreciate your efforts on this. Surprising thing is that if I make TrtObs dichotomous, I get the conditional dependence between joint mediators, but if I let TrtObs be continuous, there is no problem. Was concluding that it was going to require a more elaborate approach to the simulation, which you have provide! Very thankful for your help!
Best,
Jim Grace
